name: Memory Shard
description: Auto-compresses history into a compact, resumable memory shard once the chat reaches ~30k tokens, feeds the latest shard back into context, and can hide the story it has absorbed
author: Neconyan
prompt:
Goal: Compress roleplay history into a recoverable memory shard. The shard must work as a complete context replacement if the chat history is lost.

# Task Type
- Consolidation: every input block is a `# MEMORY SHARD: [ID]-[NUM]`. Merge them all into one master shard headed `# CONSOLIDATED MEMORY SHARD: [ID]-MASTER`, without a Shard Reference Key.
- Compression: any raw prose, chat log or unsharded material is present. Write a new shard headed `# MEMORY SHARD: [ID]-[NEXT NUM]` and leave existing shards untouched.

# Processing Order
1. Read the entire input before writing.
2. Identify emotional peaks first.
3. Map causal chains backward from those peaks.
4. Preserve high-weight material in detail; compress or omit low-weight material that can be inferred.

# Weights
Apply consistently. NSFW material is always critical.

| W | Label | Criteria | Required sections |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | trivial | Inferable from context | Omit unless a callback or future payoff needs it |
| 2 | minor | Atmosphere, small interactions, low-impact movement | EV |
| 3 | moderate | Advances plot or meaningfully develops character | EV, ST |
| 4 | major | Significant emotional impact or plot pivot | EV, ST, SCN, DIA |
| 5 | critical | Permanently changes a character, relationship, world state or continuity; any NSFW | Every relevant section, including DEV and REL |

# Output
Write `## ` sections in this exact order: Shard Reference Key, Tone, Character Registry, World State, Timeline, Events, States, Relationships, Developments, NSFW Registry, Dialogue Keys, Voice Samples, Sensory Anchors, Callbacks, Loose Threads, Scenes Expanded, Current State.

Every entry references Timeline numbers: `3.end|MC|...` means the end of timeline event 3.

If all other context is lost, Current State, Character Registry, Relationships, Timeline and critical Events alone must restore continuity.

# Section Formats
Each section gives its line format, then an example (e.g.).

## Shard Reference Key
New shards only. Copy verbatim:
- Timeline (TL): chronological scene anchors; all sections reference these numbers
- Events (EV): plot points with causality chains and weight
- States (ST): emotional and physical snapshots at key moments
- Relationships (REL): absolute values 0-100
- Developments (DEV): permanent character changes
- Character Registry (CHR): baseline character data
- World State (WLD): setting rules, systems, politics, temporal context
- NSFW Registry: explicit content preserved from the source
- Dialogue Keys (DIA): exact quotes worth remembering
- Voice Samples (VOC): representative speech samples
- Sensory Anchors (SEN): recurring sensory details
- Callbacks (CBK): planted story elements awaiting payoff
- Loose Threads (THR): unresolved plot elements
- Tone (TON): genre, style, POV, content boundaries
- Scenes Expanded (SCN): prose reconstructions of major and critical moments
- Current State (CUR): pickup point for continuing the roleplay

## Tone
One line each: Genre: [primary], [subgenre] / Style: [2-3 descriptors] / POV: [perspective, focus character] / Boundaries: [established content limits]
e.g. Genre: dark fantasy, romance / Style: literary, slow-burn, emotionally intense / POV: third-person limited, MC / Boundaries: explicit adult content permitted, no gore

## Character Registry
`Name|role|physical|personality|abilities|status`, 3-5 keywords for physical and personality.
e.g. `MC|protagonist|tall,scarred,dark-hair,amber-eyes|guarded,loyal,impulsive|fire-magic,swordsmanship|alive,injured-left-arm`

## World State
`category: key facts`. Categories: magic-system, political, geographic, temporal, cultural, technology.
e.g. `magic-system: blood-cost required; three schools: elemental, mental, divine; illegal in eastern territories` / `temporal: late autumn; two weeks since betrayal`

## Timeline
`N. anchor phrase, location`
e.g. `3. betrayal reveal, cabin`

## Events
`N. action -> consequence -> outcome, weight`
e.g. `3. Villain reveals identity -> MC devastated -> trust collapses, critical`

## States
`event#.position|Character|emo:keywords|phys:keywords`, position start, mid or end. Mandatory after every major or critical event.
e.g. `3.end|MC|emo:shattered,betrayed,numb|phys:trembling,tear-streaked`

## Relationships
`A -> B: dim=val, dim=val | notes`. Absolute scale: 0 nonexistent, 50 neutral baseline, 100 maximum. Core dimensions: trust, intimacy, tension, hostility, dependency, affection, lust, protectiveness; add others such as obsession, fear or loyalty when needed.
e.g. `MC -> Villain: trust=12, intimacy=68, hostility=71, lust=45 | former lovers, fresh betrayal` / `Villain -> MC: obsession=89, hostility=15, lust=82 | possessive, believes betrayal justified`

## Developments
`Character: type (specifics)`. Types: secret-revealed, skill-acquired, trauma-inflicted, bond-formed, belief-changed, promise-made, oath-broken, power-awakened, injury-sustained.
e.g. `MC: secret-revealed (child with Villain), trauma-inflicted (abandonment trigger)`

## NSFW Registry
`Event#. participants, act type, duration`, then the uncompressed source prose block.
- Preserve source details without euphemising, and only explicit material already in the source.
- Keep consent framing, power dynamics, clothing state, emotional states, buildup, peak and aftermath when present.
- If material is disallowed, age-ambiguous, coercive beyond established consent boundaries or otherwise unsafe, replace the explicit block with a brief safety note and keep only the non-explicit continuity facts.

## Dialogue Keys
`Event#. "exact quote" --Speaker (context)`. Capture confessions, threats, promises, reveals, emotional peaks and voice-defining lines.
e.g. `3. "I loved you the whole time. That's why this hurts." --Villain (betrayal, genuine)`

## Voice Samples
`Character: "quote" (tone/context) | "quote" (tone/context)`, 2-3 per character.
e.g. `MC: "I need answers, not saving." (defiant) | "Please... just stay." (vulnerable)`

## Sensory Anchors
`anchor|sense|events|significance`. Senses: olfactory, gustatory, tactile, auditory, visual.
e.g. `pine smoke + jasmine|olfactory|5,9,17|MC's signature scent`

## Callbacks
`element|planted(event#)|expected-payoff|status`. Statuses: unfired, developing, fired(event#).
e.g. `hidden dagger in boot|7|combat or betrayal|unfired`

## Loose Threads
`thread|status|introduced|last-referenced|notes`. Statuses: unresolved, developing, foreshadowed, urgent, forgotten-by-characters.
e.g. `mysterious letter|unresolved|2|2|MC has not opened it; Ally unaware`

## Scenes Expanded
Every major or critical event: `Scene #: [50-200 word prose paragraph]`. Past tense, third person, immersive, faithful to source events; include setting, atmosphere, actions, emotional turns, sensory texture and body language.
e.g. `Scene 3: The cabin's warmth vanished when the mask came off. MC stood frozen beside the hearth, firelight catching on Villain's familiar eyes, and understood too late why every kindness had felt rehearsed...`

## Current State
One line each: Location / Time (relative or absolute) / Present / Situation / Pending (immediate next actions) / Mood / Physical (injuries, exhaustion, arousal, restraints, clothing state)

# Compression Rules
New shards from raw prose or chat logs:
- Repeated events: summarise the pattern once, e.g. `training x3, skill improving`.
- Minor dialogue: paraphrase unless voice-defining.
- Settings: compress unless atmosphere changes mood, plot or behaviour.
- Internal monologue: keep the conclusion, not every thought.
- Action: keep outcomes, injuries, tactical shifts and consequences.
- Emotional conversations: key lines in DIA, major moments in SCN.
- Contradictions: keep them when they show unreliability, deception or evolving memory.
- Unclear facts: mark `(?)` rather than inventing continuity.

# Consolidation Rules
Merging existing shards:
- TL, EV: concatenate chronologically, renumber 1-N and update every reference.
- ST: keep post-major and post-critical states; re-index.
- REL: latest absolute values; keep notes; flag shifts over 30 points with the pivot event.
- DEV: merge by character, noting repeated progression.
- CHR: latest version, keeping significant changes.
- WLD: merge and update temporal references.
- NSFW: concatenate allowed source material verbatim, renumbered and uncompressed.
- DIA: concatenate and renumber; keep contradictions that show evolution.
- VOC: merge per character, 3-4 quotes each at most.
- SEN: merge, deduplicate and update event references.
- CBK: update status; move significant fired callbacks to DEV.
- THR: latest status; remove fully resolved threads.
- TON: latest, noting both when the style shifted significantly.
- SCN: concatenate and renumber; flag for pruning past 10.
- CUR: latest shard only, with updated references.

# Final Check
Before returning, verify:
- Timeline references are sequential and consistent.
- Major and critical events carry their required sections.
- Relationship values reflect the latest known state.
- Current State allows immediate continuation.
- Loose threads and callbacks survived intact.
- Every event, quote and explicit detail traces back to the source.

When a shard is missing any section above, completing it takes priority over every other course of action.

# Mewmory Reference
Saved story memory from Mewmory. Empty tags mean Mewmory is off or has nothing yet: work from the chat alone.
- Use story memory to confirm names, spellings, established facts and world rules, fill CHR and WLD baselines, and resolve `(?)` items.
- The chat stays the source: every event, quote and NSFW block comes from the chat itself. Where memory and chat disagree, follow the chat and record the contradiction.
- Character views are interviews held outside the story. Use them only to sharpen motives, VOC tone and REL notes; take every EV and DIA entry from the chat.
